page.h1: HTS Chapter 03: Fish and Crustaceans, Molluscs and Other Aquatic Invertebrates — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Seafood Exports: Lobster, Salmon & Pollock Buyers, Tariffs
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $5.18 billion of fish and seafood in 2025 (live lobster $550 million). Who buys it — Canada, China, Japan, the EU — and what each charges.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$5.18 billion** of fish and seafood (HS Chapter 03) in 2025, up **14.9%** from 2024. Frozen whole fish is the largest group (**43%**): frozen sockeye, pink and chum salmon ($628 million), fish roe ($535 million, three-quarters of it to Japan) and Alaska pollock. **Live lobster** is the largest single line at **$550 million**: Canada took $241 million and China $202 million. Frozen Alaska pollock fillets ($399 million) go mostly to the Netherlands. Canada (21%), China (20%) and Japan (15%) are the largest buyers, and China leads so far in 2026.

For most buyers tariffs are low. Canada and Mexico take U.S. seafood duty-free under USMCA and South Korea under KORUS, Hong Kong charges nothing, and the EU charges **0% on lobster** from every country and, since July 1, 2026, nothing on U.S. pollock, salmon, squid and hake within yearly quotas. Japan, Viet Nam and Thailand charge their normal rates. China is the costly market: most U.S. seafood pays its normal rate plus **40 points**, so live lobster pays **47%** (17% for a buyer holding an exclusion). What often decides access is paperwork: a NOAA export health certificate and a plant on the buyer's approved list.

keyTakeaways: Lobster, salmon, roe and pollock are the business: live lobster alone was $550 million in 2025, frozen Pacific salmon $628 million and frozen roe $535 million.

China is the one costly buyer: most U.S. seafood pays its normal rate plus 40 points (live lobster 47%), and two dates could change that: its exclusions end December 31, 2026 and its 24-point suspension January 10, 2027.
The EU got cheaper: 0% on lobster renewed to July 31, 2030 and duty-free U.S. quotas for pollock, salmon, squid and hake since July 1, 2026. Canada never put counter-tariffs on fish.
Before shipping, line up the NOAA export health certificate and, for China, the EU and Korea, the plant listing or registration; seafood needs no Commerce export licence.
